svg.title: Ethereum Transaction Replacement
svg.desc: Two signed transactions from the same sender and nonce compete in the transaction pool. A replacement with higher fees may be accepted by a node's policy, but cancellation is not guaranteed until one transaction is included and consumes the nonce on the canonical chain.
svg.text: Transaction Replacement — Same Nonce, New Signature
A txpool may accept a replacement if its local fee-bump policy is satisfied
Original pending transaction
sender = A · nonce = 7
Signed hash H₁ · lower fee parameters
Replacement candidate
sender = A · nonce = 7
Signed hash H₂ · higher eligible fee parameters
Node transaction pool
• Same sender + nonce creates a conflict.
• Node checks its own replacement price policy.
• Underpriced replacement can be rejected.
Replacement policy is client/network dependent.
Fee fields depend on transaction type
Legacy / type 1: gasPrice
Type 2: maxFeePerGas + maxPriorityFeePerGas
Blob tx: also consider maxFeePerBlobGas
Geth's regular txpool default bump is 10%, not a consensus rule.
Speed Up vs Cancel
Speed Up
Keep intended call/value/data; increase fee fields
Cancel attempt
Submit different payload at the same nonce
One version gets included first
Its nonce is consumed in canonical state.
The competing same-nonce version is normally
invalid against the updated account nonce.
Why "Cancel" is not guaranteed
Different peers may hold different candidates.
The original can still be included first, and a
reorg can change the canonical result.
Track both hashes. A node accepting a replacement does not prove global removal or block inclusion.
